From every clean animal take seven by seven, a male and its mate; and from the animals that are not clean, two, a male and its mate.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openscriptures/morphhb/3d15126fb1ef74867fc1434be1942e837932691f/wlc/Gen.xml · Gen.7.2

### Current best selected translation

반복수사 שבעה שבעה의 분배형태와 사람용어인 איש ואשתו의동물짝 적용을 드러낸다.한국어 일곱씩은 반복수사의분배기능을 자연스럽게옮긴다.뒤의둘은 수컷과짝을 이룬다.정결하지않은이라는부정을지켜 부정형범주를동일어휘로유지한다. 7:2의짝·수량논쟁은공개주석에유보.

#### claude-sonnet-5-5

Final opinion (Korean original): '암수 일곱 쌍'으로 잠정 정리한다.

#### gemini-3.8-flash-medium

#### gpt-6.1-sol

Final opinion (Korean original): 반복수사 שבעה שבעה의 분배형태와 사람용어인 איש ואשתו의동물짝 적용을 드러낸다.한국어 일곱씩은 반복수사의분배기능을 자연스럽게옮긴다.뒤의둘은 수컷과짝을 이룬다.정결하지않은이라는부정을지켜 부정형범주를동일어휘로유지한다. 반론: 정결한동물은 일곱쌍(14마리)인지 총일곱인지 논쟁이있다.수컷과그짝의분배를일곱에적용하면 일곱쌍이자연스러우나 반복수사만으로 숫자를곱하지는않는다.직역후보는 현대독자에게 수량을불명확하게할수있다.정결은 위생이나후대음식법 전체를뜻한다고확정못한다.בהמה범위를가축만으로 제한할지도유보. 고정WLC와Swete차이를구별하고인간전문가검수대기.

For in seven more days I will send rain upon the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe every living thing that I have made from the face of the ground.”

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openscriptures/morphhb/3d15126fb1ef74867fc1434be1942e837932691f/wlc/Gen.xml · Gen.7.4

### Current best selected translation

עוד를더로표현하고남은일곱날과사십낮·사십밤,명시1인칭주어와비내림,만들었던것을지면에서지우는행위를보존한다.יקום은문맥상생명체로번역하되존재전체의무화로확대하지않음.7:1부터발화가계속되므로이절끝에서인용닫음. 이번 후보: WLC 잠정 유지. 한국어에서도 두 사십 명시. יקום은 문맥상 살아 있는 모든 것으로 옮기되 존재물 전체라는 넓은 대안과 해석성을 밝힘.

#### claude-sonnet-5-5

#### gpt-6.1-sol

For in seven more days I will send rain upon the earth for forty days and forty nights, and I will wipe every living thing that I have made from the face of the ground.”

Final opinion (Korean original): WLC 잠정 유지. 한국어에서도 두 사십 명시. יקום은 문맥상 살아 있는 모든 것으로 옮기되 존재물 전체라는 넓은 대안과 해석성을 밝힘. 반론: יקום의 외연과 땅/지면 범위는 한 절만으로 확정 못함. 어원만으로 생물만 또는 우주 전체라고 단정 불가. 그리스어 대응도 배후 히브리어를 증명하지 않음. 인간전문가 검수 대기.

Final opinion (Korean original): '생명의 영의 숨'의 뜻으로 잠정 정리한다.

#### gemini-3.8-flash-medium

Everything in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life, of all that was on dry ground, died.

Final opinion (Korean original): 본문은 '마른 땅에 있던 모든 것 가운데 콧구멍에 생명의 숨이 있는 것은 모두 죽었다'로 잠정 채택한다. 단, 원문 히브리어에 'נְשָׁמָה(숨)'와 'רוּחַ(영/기운)'가 함께 쓰였음을 각주에 명확히 표기하여 자연화로 인한 어휘 생략 우려를 방어한다.

#### gpt-6.1-sol

Everything on dry ground in whose nostrils was the breath of the spirit of life died.

Final opinion (Korean original): Gemini의 두 어휘 보존 주장은 유효하다. 본문에서는 생명의 숨으로 자연화하고 접힌 주석에 נשמה·רוח의 두 어휘 및 직역 대안을 명시한다. 그리스어의 짧은 표현만으로 히브리어 어휘를 삭제하지 않는다. 최초원문 확정이나 인간전문가 검수 완료는 아니며 더 나은 증거가 나오면 재심사한다.

Counterargument (Korean): 자연화는 두 낱말의 표면 구분을 약화한다. 반대로 생명의 영의 숨은 동물·인간 영혼론을 오해하게 할 수 있다. 짧은 그리스어만으로 히브리어를 삭제하지 않는다.

Hebrew display (MT/WLC): וַיִּ֜מַח אֶֽת־כָּל־הַיְק֣וּם ׀ אֲשֶׁ֣ר ׀ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י הָֽאֲדָמָ֗ה מֵאָדָ֤ם עַד־בְּהֵמָה֙ עַד־רֶ֨מֶשׂ֙ וְעַד־ע֣וֹף הַשָּׁמַ֔יִם וַיִּמָּח֖וּ מִן־הָאָ֑רֶץ וַיִשָּׁ֧אֶר אַךְ־נֹ֛חַ וַֽאֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בַּתֵּבָֽה׃

He wiped out every living thing on the surface of the ground, from humans to livestock, creeping things, and the birds of the heavens. They were wiped from the earth; only Noah and those with him in the ark remained.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openscriptures/morphhb/3d15126fb1ef74867fc1434be1942e837932691f/wlc/Gen.xml · Gen.7.23

### Current best selected translation

고정 WLC 첫 능동·뒤 피동, 노아와 동반자 남음을 유지. 무주어 한국어 능동문, 영어 he·스페인어 생략주어. 주석은 말씀에 섞지 않고 원문 문자 모두 보존. 옛 보류기록의 첫 동사와 주석 위치 혼동을 정정한다. 첫 능동+목적격 את, 뒤 피동과 남음은 고정 전사·사본 핵심자음 및 인쇄 주본문과 연결된다. 무주어 능동문을 유지하고 E의 다른형·남다 동사의 점 판독 공백을 밝힌다. WLC를 교정하지 않고 잠정 선택한다.

#### gemini-3.8-flash-medium

And he wiped out every living substance that was upon the face of the ground, from man to beast, to creeping thing, and to the fowl of the heavens; and they were wiped out from the earth. And only Noah was left, and those who were with him in the ark.

Final opinion (Korean original): 본문은 '지면 위의 모든 생물을 쓸어버렸고, 사람부터 가축과 기는 것과 하늘의 새까지 땅에서 쓸려 없어졌다. 오직 노아와 그와 함께 방주 안에 있던 이들만 남았다'로 잠정 채택한다. 첫 동사의 주어 명사 부재, Swete 장치 E의 수동형 대안, 그리고 וישאר 뒤의 형태주석 이슈는 텍스트의 미해결 공백으로 주석에 상세히 남겨둔다.

## 24 · HYB.GEN.007.024

Hebrew display (MT/WLC): וַיִּגְבְּר֥וּ הַמַּ֖יִם עַל־הָאָ֑רֶץ חֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּמְאַ֖ת יֽוֹם׃

The waters prevailed over the earth for one hundred and fifty days.

Source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openscriptures/morphhb/3d15126fb1ef74867fc1434be1942e837932691f/wlc/Gen.xml · Gen.7.24

### Current best selected translation

우세가 지속됨을 세력을 떨쳤다로 유지. 그리스어 높아짐 표현은 대안으로 보존. 40일과 150일의 포함관계 계산은 추가하지 않는다. 150일 동안 우세가 지속된다는 표현을 유지하고 수위가 매일 상승했다고 확정하지 않는다. 그리스어 높아짐 표현 및 세력을 떨쳤다는 한국어의 문어성은 반론으로 보존한다.

#### claude-sonnet-5-5

And the waters prevailed on the earth a hundred and fifty days.

Final opinion (Korean original): 현재 번역을 잠정안으로 둔다.

#### gemini-3.8-flash-medium

And the waters prevailed upon the earth a hundred and fifty days.

Final opinion (Korean original): '물이 백오십 일 동안 땅 위에서 세력을 떨쳤다'를 최종 채택한다. '세력을 떨쳤다'의 어휘적 방어 가능성을 확정하되, 그리스어역본의 '높아졌다'는 대안 표현과 150일의 연대기적 해석 문제는 주석과 공백 항목으로 보존한다.

#### gpt-6.1-sol

Final opinion (Korean original): 150일 동안 우세가 지속된다는 표현을 유지하고 수위가 매일 상승했다고 확정하지 않는다. 그리스어 높아짐 표현 및 세력을 떨쳤다는 한국어의 문어성은 반론으로 보존한다. 최초원문 확정이나 인간전문가 검수 완료는 아니며 더 나은 증거가 나오면 재심사한다.

Counterargument (Korean): 물이 세력을 떨쳤다는 말은 의인화처럼 보일 수 있다. 150일 동안 계속 상승했다는 해석은 별도 판정 필요.

## Notes

Verse 1 preserves I have seen, righteous, before me and this generation, while including the whole household. Verse 2 retains distributive seven by seven with a male and its mate. Seven pairs (fourteen animals) is a strong reading when the pair is distributed, but seven in total remains an alternative; the wording does not fix a total. Repeated sevens and male/female in the Greek edition do not settle the question. Cleanliness criteria, later sacrifice and harmonization with chapter 6 are not inserted.

Input is pinned WLC4.20/OSHB. Swete1901 p.10 is a modern scholarly edition of an ancient version. Leningrad4v was inspected for limited consonantal phrases only, not every vowel, accent or Masoretic note. Modern apparatus and full witness collation remain pending.

WLC verse 3 does not explicitly distinguish clean from unclean birds. The inspected Swete1901 edition does: clean birds by sevens, unclean birds by twos. Whether this longer Greek reflects another Hebrew Vorlage or harmonizing expansion remains unresolved. WLC remains provisional. Seven pairs is a strong reading, but a total of seven remains an alternative; distributive sevens are retained and seed is rendered as offspring.

Verse 4 distinguishes seven more days and forty days and forty nights. Every living thing interprets yequm contextually; everything that exists is a broader alternative. Verse 5 does not establish immediacy, inner motives or absolute sinlessness. Verse 6 retains age six hundred and floodwaters upon the earth. Swete main text lacks a water noun here; an addition appears in its apparatus, but its manuscript attribution is unverified. Because of in verse 7 has a fleeing-from alternative; no entry date, water level, headcount or geological extent is supplied.

For verses 3–7, Swete1901 pp.10–11 were directly read and limited consonantal phrases inspected in a Leningrad4v photograph. Full manuscripts, vowels, accents, Masoretic notes and modern apparatus or other Hebrew witnesses remain uncollated. Pinned WLC is an electronic transcription, not proof of the earliest wording or independent witness consensus.

Verses 8–9 retain the connected list and movement two by two. Swete1901 p.11 has a longer distinction between clean and unclean birds, absent in pinned WLC. Its Hebrew background and origin remain unresolved; WLC is retained provisionally. Two by two does not fix the total at two or harmonize it with sevens.

In verse 11 pinned WLC and the inspected consonantal wording of Leningrad4v have day seventeen of the second month. Swete1901 p.11 reads twenty-seven and lacks a main-text equivalent for great in great deep. These differences are preserved; without established grounds to replace the Hebrew input, seventeen and great deep remain provisional. This does not prove their priority. No calendar conversion, full flood duration or geological mechanism is added.

Verse 10 marks the seven days and the state of floodwaters; verse 12 describes rain for forty days and forty nights. A fixed intensity contrast between geshem and matar was not established, so rain is retained. Inspection was limited to Swete and consonantal phrases in Leningrad. Modern apparatus, other Hebrew witnesses including Samaritan texts and 4Q252, other ancient versions and specialist review remain pending.

Verses 13–15 preserve the family and animal lists, the four repetitions of according to kind, movement two by two and the breath of life. Kind is not a modern taxonomic species. In verse 14, they and every bird/every winged thing are in pinned Hebrew and the inspected Leningrad consonants, with no corresponding phrases in Swete1901 p.11. The longer Hebrew is retained provisionally; a different Vorlage or Greek abbreviation remains unresolved. In verse 13 Hebrew has with them and Swete with him; the source of the difference is unresolved. Entered in verse 14 is supplied from verse 13. Every wing is interpreted as every winged thing; every bird of every kind of wing is an alternative.

Verse 16 distinguishes God commanding from YHWH closing. Shut him in interprets beʿado in context; behind him or for him are alternatives. The Hebrew does not specify a door, the ark as object, or an outside position. Swete explicitly has Lord God, the ark and outside him. Whether this reflects another Hebrew text or explanatory translation remains unresolved.

In verse 17 pinned Hebrew and the inspected Leningrad consonants read forty days; Swete1901 p.11 reads forty days and forty nights. Rösel (1998) interprets this as harmonization with 7:12, which does not prove its origin. Hebrew without the added nights is retained provisionally, while the possibility of an earlier longer reading remains open. Rising waters and the ark rising are preserved; the end of the whole flood is not fixed. Modern apparatus, other Hebrew witnesses, full ancient-version collation and specialist review remain pending.

Verses 18–19 preserve the waters gaining strength and increasing, the ark moving over the water, emphatic intensity, and all high mountains being covered. Moved in verse 18 renders a general motion verb; floated is a contextual alternative. Under the whole heaven is retained without deciding modern geographical extent. Pinned Hebrew and the inspected Leningrad consonants have repeated emphasis and all before heaven; Swete1901 p.11 has one emphatic adverb and no all before heaven. Another Vorlage or translation concision remains unresolved. Modern apparatus, wider collation and human specialist review are pending.

Verses 20–24 retain the pinned WLC provisionally. Fifteen cubits above the mountains is a strong contextual reading; the reference point is not supplied in the translation. In verse 22, breath of life naturalizes the overlapping Hebrew breath/spirit wording, whose literal alternative is breath of the spirit of life. Verse 23 retains the initial active and later passive without supplying a divine name. The plain XML form note follows the remain verb, not the initial wipe verb; all WLC codepoints remain unchanged. Swete1901 p.12 has shorter wording in verse 22 and a different initial verb form marked E in its verse 23 apparatus. The E witness identification and modern apparatus are unverified. Only limited consonantal phrases in Leningrad4v/5r were inspected; full collation and specialist review remain pending.
